content.text: Gastric Tubes
Orogastric Tube (OGT):
CM-EX: corner of mouth -earlobe  -xyphoid
Pros:    -   lrg diameter poss ->preferred for rapid GI decontamination
Cons:    -   ↓comfortable & ⍉well tolerated          -   vomiting very common    **
UNCONSCIOUS ->  INTUBATED
Avg length:  teeth to stomach
Avg range of orogastric tube lengths
NGT -MC gastric tube
Pros:     -   Better tolerance for chronic                          -   ↓risk of emesis       -    NOT NEED INTUBATION
Cons:    -   nasal anatomy can limit placement              -    Limited tube size
Indication to place:
GI bleed                                             -    multi-system trauma: need to empty stomach to prevent aspiration
Diverticulitis: give bowel a rest     -    GI contamination: gastric lavage
Pancreatitis: give bowel a rest      -    admin med: check if ok for pills to be crushed
near drowning                                 -    aspiration of GI contents for diagnostics
temp enteral feeding                      -    acute gastric dilation or distention
bowel obstruct                                 -    Ileus
Burns: Lrg: -
lrg loss of fluid & K -> ↓smooth muscle contraction ->  gastroparesis & ileus
Relative Contraindications:
Coagulopathy                                           -    ↑intracranial P -control cough & retching
deviated septum                                      -    recent esophageal surgery w/in 6M
bariatric surgery -depend on type        -    recent nasal surgery w/in 6M
Absolute Contraindications
sus esophageal laceration or perforation           -    esophageal tumor or stricture
Ingest caustic substance -disrupt esophagus     -    mid-facial fractures
Equipment:
gloves, mask, gown, eye protection   -  appropriate NGT       -  light source      -  emesis basin     -    Tape
wall suction w regulator        -  water soluble lube                -  water & straw    -    vasoconstrict nasal spray
topical anesthetic spray or gel           -   warm 0.9 NS for lavage     -  60 cc cath tip syringe    -    Stethoscope
B4 Placement
Pt ed on procedure
considerations for consent:
Location’s policy (check): written vs verbal consent     -    Pt capacity to consent or cooperate
Additional person -help or sedate or restrain
Precautions: REQUIRED -
STRD PRECAUTIONS -clean procedure
Preparation
Positioning:
high fowler's position -> sitting u
p
Avoid if pt neck =extended -> NGT in airway
Tube size: # ↑ w diameter                                       *Avg =5-18FR,
⍉ +18Fr b/c P sores & epistaxis
Tube Length: enure placement:
NEX: nose, ear, xiphoid -> mark line w tape
Adult tubes = 50in long           -markers @ 18, 22, 26, 30 in  OR 45, 55, 66, 76 cm
Underestimate tube length = in esophagus, ⍉ stomach
Overestimate tube length = duodenum, ⍉stomach
Tube Rigidity: Semi-rigid -> too rigid = P sores on nasal passages
Make tube less flexible: soak in ice water for 1-2 min
Lube options:
Surgilube  &  lidocaine jelly: ⍉count as nasopharyngeal anesthesia
Petroleum based products: CONTRAINDICATED
trachea placement w petroleum -> chemical pneumonitis ->
needs to water soluble
Anesthesia: nasopharyngeal anesthesia makes or breaks successful placement
Clin Uses:     -    ↓pain             -    suppress gag reflex
Usually missed b/c techs prep -cannot give meds
Locations that need anesthesia: nose AND P. pharynx
***ASK ABOUT “CAINE” ALLERGIES B4 ANESTH****
Hurricane or Cetacaine spray
-   Spray P. oropharynx
Only effect mucosa
-  onset 1 min    -   duration 1 hr    -  max dose = 2sec spray
Lidocaine Jelly 2%
- Pt =supine -> few cc's drip down nasal passage & bathe P. oropharynx
onset of action 5 min                           -    duration 1 hr
Topical Vasoconstrictors (ex. afrin):
CAUTION IN PT W HTN
-  lrg diameter for placement
-   ↓mucosal congestion    -  make placement easier    -  controls bleeding       -  ↓mucosal trauma
Placement
1st Step:
nose, oral, throat exam
check B/L nasal patency -deviated septum, polyps, clots, bleeding, congested mucosa
check throat: tonsillar or adenoid enlrg
2nd step: tuck chin to chest
3rd step: have pt sip water
No swallow technique: ↑1st time placement success
pt =deep breath & hold  ->glottis closes & ↓risk of endotracheal placement
No swallow technique issues:
Poss trigger gag reflex & cause cough       -    pt may ⍉hold breath long enough
4th step. gently insert tube in nose
inspect mouth during NGT placement: ensure tube ⍉coiling
hug floor of nose & I. turbinate
⍉bounce off S. turbinate -> tube curls up or damage nasal mucosa
5th step. While pt swallows water -> advance quickly w gentle P to predetermined depth
Confirm Placement:
policy -> NGT placement confirmed w radiograph b4 used for feeding
CXR, CT, POCUS post-place                                             -    observe for gastric fluid - use syringe to pull & see
attach CO2 monitor: stay purple                                   -    insufflate air into tube & listen for borborygmi
test pH of fluid (pH < 4 means gastric placement)    -    have pt speak - =⍉ in lungs -vocal cords work
Effects:
Lyte disturbances:
hypokalemia   -  metabolic alkalosis -check pH
endobronchial tube placement         -    mucosal damage from improper suctioning         -    Sinusitis
perforation of cribriform plate, nasopharynx, esophagus            -   otitis media                  -    Epistaxis
Removal
When: ⍉medically indicated
How: strd precautions, pull w slow gentle traction
IMMEDIATE REMOVAL:        -    severe coughing       -    gagging                  -    voice changes    -   can't speak
tube is coiling     -    resp distress              -    ↑pt agitation       -    hypoxia on pulse ox
Gastric Lavage
MOA: clear stomach contents -> lavage until clear
instill
at a time during gastric lavage ->avoid distention or emesis
Preferred Position: LLDP    - ⍉ always practical b/c trauma
tube usually below stomachs fluid meniscus-> ↓emptying into duodenum & ↓risk of aspiration
CONTRAINDICATED: RLDP    -> tube above fluid meniscus & encourages pyloric emptying
Solution =warm 0.9NS or warm tap water
***NEVER COLD SALINE -> ↓CORE BODY TEMP***
Clin Use: Confirms active bleeding b/c blood returns during lavage
Suction: rest stomach & bowel
Intermittent suction -> hicky, sores, bleeding
P:      HIGH: 120-200 mmHg          MED: 80-120 mmHg          LOW: 0-80 mmHg -> lowest suction for job
Activated Charcoal:
Activated charcoal
= ±sorbitol (laxative)
ASK WHEN PT INGEST SOMETHING:     WHEN   &  WHERE
Use: min systemic drug or poison absorb <- binds to some substances
Can drink if intact gag reflex,
most effective 0-2hr post-ingest
Substances absorbed by activated charcoal: ABCDs
antimalarials (quinine), aminophylline (theophylline), poss ASA
barbiturates (phenobarbital), BB (nadolol)
carbamazepine
dapsone, dilantin
Substances NOT absorb by activated charcoal: PHAILS
Pesticides    - Hydrocarbons   -  acids, alkali     -  iron     -  lithium    -   solvents
Multi-dose Charcoal: ↓1/2 life of drugs that undergo extensive enterohepatic recirculation
Dosing
absorbs 100 - 1,000 mg of drug/poison per gram of charcoal
25g per 120 ml of Activated charcoal       -    1g of charcoal per 1 kg
adults should have sorbitol                       -   peds should not have sorbitol
Influences of substance absorb in GI tract
amount or vol           -    medium of delivery      -    time in GI tract        -    GI motility     -    length of GI tract
